summary: Oxytocin almost doubled within five minutes of listening to 528 Hz music. The increase with 440 Hz music was not statistically significant. Mean saliva levels rose from 37.57 to 73.58 pg/mL in the 528 Hz condition (p < 0.038). Cortisol also fell later after 528 Hz music.
limitation: Nine healthy adults took part. These short-term saliva findings need independent replication in larger samples.
description: A small, active research field with promising findings for short-term stress and anxiety.
paragraphs: Oxytocin almost doubled within five minutes of listening to 528 Hz music in the 2018 study; the increase with 440 Hz music was not statistically significant. Other studies report reductions in anxiety, cortisol and blood pressure.

Several randomized trials now complement the earlier human and laboratory studies. The evidence remains preliminary: samples are generally small, blinding and reporting vary, follow-up is short, and some outcomes show no significant change.
